title: Toward recursive self-improvement: how GLM built its own inference infrastructure
gist: An agent powered by GLM-5.3 did much of the work of bringing a GLM-5.3 variant from first run to production on a large cluster of Chinese-made accelerators. The stated key is dense feedback: correctness comparisons, microbenchmarks, traces and end-to-end metrics packaged as repeatable workflows the agent can call.
changes: The most literal instance of the recursive framing: a model optimising the serving of its own family, on chips where no mature kernel library exists. It also says outright that this is not yet RSI.
caveats: Self-reported and mostly unverifiable. The 3x is against the team's own first port. Engineers set objectives, built the feedback environment and reviewed anything touching architecture, concurrency or production risk; the human share is not quantified.

bears_on.note: A model family building its own serving stack. The authors themselves say they are not there yet.
New accelerators with no kernel ecosystem are where hand-tuning cannot keep up.
The enabler was dense feedback, and people built it.
